# Razobill

> Razobill is an open-source log parser (C++20, Apache 2.0) that splits each log line into a template plus typed values (integers and strings) and rebuilds the exact original line from them. It ships as pyrazobill (Python), a DuckDB extension, and a C API. Current version: 1.1.1.

The name is spelled "Razobill". Its mascot is a razorbill, a seabird.

## Key facts
- Lossless: 0 mismatches across a 69.6 million line audit (4,861 log files, 6.82 GB), measured by the project author.
- Install: `pip install pyrazobill` (Python 3.9 to 3.13; Windows, Linux, macOS).
- Python API: `rz.RzSplit(line)` returns a named tuple `(template, ints, strs)`. Templates contain `{i}` and `{s}` placeholders. `rz.RzJoin(*record)` returns the exact original line bit-for-bit.
- DuckDB API: `SELECT RzSplit(line)` returns `STRUCT(template VARCHAR, ints BIGINT[], strs VARCHAR[])`. `SELECT RzJoin(...)` restores raw bytes.
- Versus Drain3: 2.5x to 15.1x faster on one thread across five LogHub datasets. Drain3 scored higher on median grouping accuracy (0.871 vs 0.808); Razobill keeps every value and restores exact bytes.
- Theory: Atta, M. M. (2026), "Latitude and Doubt", Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23287286.
- Known limits: benchmarks are author-run; S3 results use emulators; the DuckDB community listing is a pending pull request (duckdb/community-extensions #3023).
